headlines.title: 베선트 " 원화 변동성 목격"…엔화 이어 한국도 직접 거론

headlines.title: 살릴 기업 못 살리는 기업회생법 [H-EXCLUSIVE]

key_headlines.title: Real Estate Tax Reform: Different Criteria for Each Tax Type
key_headlines.summary: The government's real estate tax overhaul maintains current acquisition and property taxes while adjusting capital gains tax to emphasize actual residency, with varying deduction standards based on home ownership and residency status.

key_headlines.title: Landlords Returning to Primary Residences Trigger Jeonse Crisis
key_headlines.summary: Non-resident property owners are reversing plans to rent out properties due to higher holding taxes, exacerbating Seoul's housing shortage as jeonse (charter) inventory disappears and prices spike to near 700 million won average.

key_headlines.title: Morgan Stanley Raises Korea's 2026 Growth Forecast to 3.4%
key_headlines.summary: Morgan Stanley upgraded Korea's economic outlook, projecting 3.4% growth for 2026 and expecting the central bank to raise the policy rate to 3.5% by Q1 2027 due to stronger-than-expected economic recovery.

key_headlines.title: Kospi Surges 3.76% as Market Rebounds from Extreme Pessimism
key_headlines.summary: The Korean stock market rebounded sharply following U.S. stock strength and semiconductor sector gains, with Kospi breaking 6,600 as investors gain confidence after last month's market bottom.

key_headlines.title: SK Telecom Q2 Operating Profit Jumps 67% on AI Data Center Growth
key_headlines.summary: SK Telecom posted strong Q2 earnings with operating profit of 566 billion won, driven by a doubling of AI data center revenues as the company recovers from prior security incidents.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's real estate sector faces significant challenges following the government's tax reform announcement. While the tax system aims to stabilize the property market through differentiated rates based on residency and ownership, it has triggered unintended consequences including a surge in non-resident property holders returning to primary residences and a severe shortage of jeonse (charter) properties. Seoul's average jeonse prices have climbed to approximately 700 million won with monthly rent reaching 1.6 million won, creating financial hardship for renters. The government is expected to announce measures to expand housing supply in the metropolitan area to address the worsening housing crisis. Industry experts emphasize that the fundamental solution requires increased private housing supply rather than tax increases alone.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Morgan Stanley has significantly upgraded its economic outlook for Korea, raising the 2026 growth forecast by 0.6 percentage points to 3.4% and projecting the Bank of Korea will accelerate policy rate increases to 3.5% by Q1 2027. The stronger-than-expected economic recovery is driving inflation pressures that necessitate faster monetary tightening than originally anticipated. South Korea's tourism sector continues to show robust performance, with foreign visitor spending contributing four times more to GDP growth post-COVID compared to earlier periods. Meanwhile, India's central bank held rates steady at 5.25% while maintaining a 6.7% GDP growth forecast, indicating divergent monetary policy paths across Asia.
sections.Financial Markets: Korean stock markets staged a significant rally with Kospi jumping 3.76% to 6,598.26, driven by positive momentum from U.S. markets where the S&P 500 reached new all-time highs. Semiconductor stocks led the rebound, with analysts crediting overnight strength in Western Digital and Sandisk earnings as key catalysts for continued market recovery. The won-dollar exchange rate weakened to 1,424.5 won as risk appetite improved and oil prices fell amid Middle East tensions easing. Market participants believe the domestic stock market confirmed its bottom in July and expect continued recovery throughout August.
sections.Industry & Technology: Korea's semiconductor sector continues to dominate market movements as investors gain confidence in chip-related companies. Analog semiconductor specialist Hatchek announced plans for Kosdaq listing targeting the global market, while corporate credit growth concentrated heavily in semiconductor, shipbuilding, and defense industries. The government's green energy and electric vehicle incentive programs face criticism for leaving out electric vehicle production tax credits and low-carbon steel investment support, putting Korean companies at a disadvantage compared to Japanese counterparts. Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology represents an emerging opportunity where Korea's semiconductor, sensor, and medical technology strengths position the nation competitively in this convergence field.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's real estate market faces mounting pressure as the government's tax reform drives unintended consequences including a collapse in jeonse inventory and soaring prices. Non-resident property owners declaring their return to primary residences is exacerbating the housing shortage, while renters face severe affordability challenges with average jeonse reaching near 700 million won. Busan presents a contrasting picture with positive market fundamentals, as real estate prices rose 0.48% year-over-year with strong demand from real-use buyers concentrated in preferred neighborhoods around Haeundae and Daeyon-dong. High school district location (school districts) emerged as the primary driver of apartment pre-leasing competition, replacing metro accessibility as the key factor attracting buyers in provincial markets.
sections.International Economy: U.S. Treasury Secretary and Japan's Finance Minister are publicly pressuring their respective central banks, with the U.S. seeking Federal Reserve emergency liquidity expansion and Japan requesting aggressive Bank of Japan support for government debt purchases. The Dow Jones reached all-time highs while crude oil prices declined sharply, prompting a 6 basis point drop in 10-year Treasury yields to 4.68% as market expectations for September Fed rate hikes stand at 66.5%. Currency markets reflect tensions in international monetary policy coordination, with the won strengthening against the dollar to 1,424.5 won amid easing Middle East tensions and falling oil prices. The CME FedWatch tool indicates 58.4% probability of a 25 basis point Fed rate increase in mid-September.
sections.AI & Economy: SpaceX entered the AI infrastructure competition with massive investments, reporting Q2 revenues of 7.8 billion dollars while investing 18.37 billion dollars in capital expenditures, with 15.8 billion dollars directed toward AI data center construction set to begin in 2027. Amazon crossed the 3 trillion dollar market capitalization milestone, driven by robust cloud infrastructure growth serving surging AI demand, while Microsoft similarly benefits from Azure's strong performance. The South Korean government announced a 1 trillion won AI infrastructure fund through joint investment by Industrial Bank of Korea and Korea Post Office, each contributing 500 billion won for data center and green power grid projects. SK Telecom posted 67% operating profit growth in Q2 with AI data center revenues doubling, demonstrating the commercial viability of AI infrastructure investments despite earlier market skepticism.
sections.Others: Single-stock leveraged ETF trading volumes collapsed from 12 trillion won to below 1 trillion won within one week following regulatory tightening measures, suggesting enhanced trading restrictions are effectively reducing market participation. The United States, Iran, and Oman are reportedly close to negotiating terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, potentially easing global oil supply concerns. Denmark significantly expanded its conscription program in response to Russian security threats and U.S. pressure regarding Greenland, with even royal family members now subject to military service requirements. The Korea Internet and Security Agency revised its blockchain project evaluation methods to focus more on actual economic impact beyond employment creation metrics. BigValue opened 5.15 million pages of data to improve AI accessibility, recognizing that AI-friendly data presentation has become a competitive advantage in the digital economy.
